$comment: Documented, EXPIRING exceptions for scripts/audit-gate.mjs (ported from
molecule 2026-10-03 after the same bare-audit wall). Every advisory still
fails CI unless it is listed here by its GHSA id and unexpired. An entry is a
risk decision with a date on it, not a mute button: when expires passes the
gate goes red again so the decision gets remade. Never add an entry to make a
build green — add it only when there is no upstream fix AND the exposure is

accepted.package: braces (via micromatch -> oclif/find-yarn-workspace-root, fast-glob -> shelljs -> shx)
accepted.reason: Stack-exhaustion DoS in braces when compiling a deeply-nested glob pattern (advisory published 2026-09-18T18:31Z — mlcl CI went red on it on the 2026-10-03 pin-sweep push). NO upstream fix exists: the advisory range is braces <= 3.0.3 with first_patched_version null — every released version is vulnerable, and npm audit reports the only remediation as a DOWNGRADE of oclif to 1.16.1 (2018), which is arborist picking an older tree without micromatch, not a patched chain. Dev-only by reachability: the chain lives in mlcl devDependencies (the oclif CLI toolchain and shell-script helpers); mlcl ships no runtime dependencies that carry it, and the DoS requires feeding a crafted nested glob to the matcher — here the patterns are mlcl’s own fixed template globs, not attacker input. Residual risk: a future tooling change that passes external input as a glob would re-expose it; the gate goes red again at expiry so the decision gets remade. Re-check at expiry for a patched braces release or a chain without it, bump, and drop this entry.

max-stale handling can disclose cross-user cached responses (advisory on http-cache-semantics <= 4.2.0 with NO patched release — every version ever published is in range). Reached only through the oclif devDependency (oclif -> got 13 -> cacheable-request 10 -> http-cache-semantics 4.1.x), which mlcl uses at development time for its own CLI tooling; the published mlcl package carries none of it (@oclif/core and plugin-help, the runtime deps, pull no got). The disclosure requires a SHARED HTTP cache across users on one machine with crafted max-stale responses — not a shape oclif update checks produce. npm reports the only remediation as a downgrade to oclif 1.16.1 (2018), which is an older tree without got, not a fixed chain. Residual risk: a future refactor adding runtime HTTP caching through got would re-expose it; the gate goes red again at expiry so the decision gets remade. Re-check at expiry for a patched http-cache-semantics or a cacheable-request release without it, bump, and drop this entry.
